title: Heaters
statement:
Houses and heaters stand at integer points on a straight line: `houses[i]` is the position of a house and `heaters[j]` the position of a heater. Every heater is given the same warming radius `r`, and a heater at `x` warms every house whose position is between `x - r` and `x + r` inclusive. Return the smallest integer `r` for which every house is warmed by at least one heater.

Neither array is necessarily sorted, and positions may repeat.
notes:
## Intuition

Each house only cares about its nearest heater, and the radius must reach the farthest of those nearest distances: the answer is the maximum, over houses, of the distance to the closest heater. Checking every heater for every house costs O(n·m). Once `heaters` is sorted, the closest heater to a house is one of its two neighbours in sorted order, and binary search finds them in O(log m).

## Approach

1. Sort `heaters`.
2. For each `house`, binary search for `left`, the first index with `heaters[left] >= house` (it equals `heaters.length` when every heater is to the left).
3. `after = heaters[left] - house` is the gap to the nearest heater at or to the right; `before = house - heaters[left - 1]` is the gap to the nearest heater on the left. A missing side counts as `Infinity`.
4. The house needs `Math.min(before, after)`; keep the largest such value in `radius`.
5. Return `radius`.

## Example 1, step by step

`houses = [1,2,3]`, `heaters = [2]`. House `1`: `left = 0`, `after = 2 - 1 = 1`, no heater before, so it needs `1`. House `2`: `left = 0`, `after = 0`, so it needs `0`. House `3`: `left = 1` (past the end), `before = 3 - 2 = 1`, so it needs `1`. The largest need is `radius = 1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n + m) log m): sorting the `m` heaters, then one binary search per house.
- Space: O(1) beyond the sort.

## Pitfalls

- The inputs are not sorted; sort `heaters` before searching (sorting `houses` is not needed).
- Sort numerically with `(a, b) => a - b`; the default sort compares strings.
- A house may lie before the first heater or after the last one; guard both indices.
- The answer is the maximum of per-house minimums, not the largest gap between heaters.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `radius` | the largest distance any house so far needs |
| `house` | the house being placed |
| `left`, `right` | binary-search bounds; `left` ends at the first heater `>= house` |
| `mid` | the middle index being tested |
| `after`, `before` | distances to the nearest heater on the right and on the left |

narration.2: Sort the heaters numerically so binary search can find each house's neighbours.
narration.3: The radius must cover the neediest house; start from 0.
narration.4: Handle the houses one at a time; their order does not matter.
narration.7: Binary search for the first heater at or to the right of the house.
narration.8: Look at the middle of the remaining range.
narration.9: This heater is left of the house, so the answer lies further right.
narration.10: Skip mid and everything before it.
narration.12: heaters[mid] is a candidate, so keep it inside the range.
narration.15: Gap to the nearest heater at or after the house, if there is one.
narration.16: Gap to the nearest heater before the house, if there is one.
narration.17: The house needs the smaller gap; the radius must be at least that.
narration.19: The largest need over all houses is the smallest radius that warms them all.
